notes.title: Bot Hunter Release
notes.notes:
Hello Hunters!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45106431/00fbbb22c4fb3c480df9aef2fdf68d44d3e3b2e8.gif[/img]

We're excited to announce that Bot Hunter is released now! We still can't believe this is really happening and we've managed to finish this project and release our first game. We learned a lot while working on Bot Hunter and we wish to continue growing in game developement.

Huge thanks to everyone who has been with us on this journey! We really appeciate your support. Your opinions and feedback helped us balance the game and make it so much better.

Please don't forget to leave a review after playing Bot Hunter! This would mean a lot to us!

notes.title: Dev Update #6
notes.notes:
Hello Hunters!

The Bot Hunter release is near so here's a little update.

In the previous update we have added 2 new magazines: Ripper and Plasma Ball. Now we have made a dedicated type of guns for each of them as well as new shotgun model. You can now notice the enemies holding them so you know what to expect from their attacks.

We have recieved messages pointing out that the game balance needs improving. We made some changes so player's weapon is now overheating slower and enemies are a bit more easier to kill. Let us know what you think of the gameplay now.

To help player in the later stages of the game we added higher tier to some weapon modules.

Speaking of the weapon modules - we have decided to grant access to sandbox game mode in the full version of Bot Hunter. It lets you try out all the different weapons possible to craft in the game. 

As you know from the update #5 we were rewriting the Bot Hunter plotline. It is finished and includes a complete questline. Now you will be playing as a bounty hunter for the misterious task giver with an ambition to establish order in the injust bot society. During your playthrough you will encounter 4 unique bosses, each having its own model.

For the other changes:
[list]
[*] Gamepad improvements: the game is now pausing after disconnecting the controller and while using Steam overlay
[*] Fixing the bug causing game crash after trying to use crafting station before unlocking any crafting recipes
[*] Gameplay rebalance
[*] Coloring enemies health bars with the color of their armor so it is easier to distinguish which weapon color to attack them with
[*] Adding a sounds to new projectiles
[*] New boss arenas for the other 4 planets (available in full version)
[/list]

All of the gameplay improvment you can check out now in the Bot Hunter Demo but there you can only play on the first planet. The rest of them as well as the full storyline will only be available in the [b]full version of the game that will be released on April 7th.[/b]

notes.title: Dev Update #5
notes.notes:
Hello Hunters!

It’s time for a small review of what we have done recently. 

We focused on improving Bot Hunter’s storyline that you could experience through the chat with the mysterious contract giver. We felt it was a little bit too plain so we did some brainstorming and formed a complete story with a questline assigned to it. It has much more depth now and it gives meaning to the gameplay. This resulted in the updated Demo version 0.1.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45106431/fd523a7f118a5a1ec8c9f17fcb553ea626c6d19a.png[/img]

Unfortunately, storyline changes were so significant we had to WIPE THE SAVES… BUT the demo version 0.0 will still be available on its own Steam branch if some of you would like to continue their game there. We’ve prepared a quick tutorial if you had a problem with switching branches.

To change the Steam branch:
[olist]
[*] Right click on Bot Hunter Demo in your Steam library 
[*] Choose “Properties…”
[*] In the Properties window choose “Betas” in the tabs on the left
[*] In “Beta Participation” toggle list choose “version_0.0 - version 0.0” (or “None” if you want to go back to the newest version)
[/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45106431/314c1eadda97a01cad1bfa6ac6c5faa9e56947e0.png[/img]

We would also like to remind you that we will participate in the February edition of Steam Next Fest! We will be so grateful if you would support us by checking the Next Fest version of Bot Hunter Demo and share your feedback with us. It is very important as it allows us to maximally improve Bot Hunter before its release in April. 

For the other changes:
[list]
[*] Adding 2 new weapon magazines: Ripper and Plasma Ball
[*] Improving the enemies’ movement
[*] Adding new attacks for higher levels enemies 
[*] Fixing issue with boss HP (due to some earlier NPC spawning optimization, bosses HP didn’t scale with contract level so they were ridiculously easy to kill on higher level contracts)
[*] TankBot movement improvement
[/list]

Thank you for being here! See you in the next update!

notes.title: Dev Update #4
notes.notes:
Hello Hunters!

Public Playtest was a big milestone in Bot Hunter journey and it lead us to even bigger one: Bot Hunter Demo. This time we were polishing the tiny details and now we are ready to release the demo for you!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45106431/1f4b3a5f3ad247c9057a811a323bbd4034c37c50.gif[/img]

The most notable changes we've made are:
[list]
[*] Improving player weapon model (we've made it more detailed and contrasting)
[*] Introducing player's armor that increases max HP and adds variation to player model
[*] Making tutorials more readable and ordering them better
[*] Improving death and beam up vfx
[*] Fixing issue with light bleeding between rooms and stars being visible through tiny gaps between chunks
[*] Fixing long-living bug that made player stuck in closed room without any enemy to kill
[*] Fixing bug with hack panel being disabled after reentering the room
[*] Rebalancing enemy HP and how much loot you gather
[/list]

Oh! We kinda lied about tiny changes only. We've also added two new enemies TankBot and StormEye and new Weapon Module: Lightning.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45106431/8609e5f85d241da6eb8c0516a926c560dbf8b607.png[/img]

And that's all in terms of changes. Now we're getting ready for the Next Fest. We can't wait to hear what you think about Demo.

Thank you all for being with us on this journey!

notes.title: Dev Update #3
notes.notes:
Hello Hunters!

We're in the middle of playtest and we've received lots of valuable feedback from you for which we are super grateful! Many of you pointed out that Bot Hunter's movement and shooting need to be more dynamic. We've tested a few options and have chosen the one we think will be the most satisfying.

Now each Jump and Dash increases your max speed up to some cap. Than it gradually decreases. While you're moving with high velocity not only you deal greater damage but also receive less of it.

We've put a lot of efforts into improving camera movement. It's much smoother now what helps to feel the momentum of your bot. What's more when you receive a hit the camera will shake.

To make combat more dynamic we've increased each projectile damage. If you are speeding and your weapon has matching color you will kill basic enemies with one precise hit now.

Because of this big changes in movement we decided to PROLONG PLAYTEST to January 12th, so everyone will have a chance to try them out. You can request access to it on our store page and it will pop up in your library immediately.

Let us know how the new movement feels!

Cheers

Hello Hunters!

Public Playtest is finally here and it will be available until 5th January!

Request access on our store page and Bot Hunter Playtest will appear in your library. You can install and launch it from there.

This build contains two game modes
[olist]
[*] New Game - tutorial that explains basics of the game including Color Theory, Crafting System and Contract Progression
[*] Sandbox - that lets you experiment with game mechanics
[/olist]
This is alpha version so you may encounter some bugs and imperfections. You can report them on our [url=https://discord.gg/XPvPjzERBF]Discord Server[/url]. We'd also love to hear your feedback there.

Let's improve the Bot Hunter together!
See you on our Discord!

EDIT: Due to big changes we've made based on you feedback we decided to PROLONG PLAYTEST until 12th January!

notes.title: Crafting System
notes.notes:
Hello Hunters!

One of the core mechanics in Bot Hunter is its unique Crafting System. It allows you to create a wide variety of guns from simple modules. Everything from Blaster Pistol to Fully Automatic Shotgun Rocket Launcher. 

The weapon is a reflection of your progress. You do not level-up, you need to craft better modules instead. It is crucial to understand how weapon modules will interact with each other so we’ve made this Crafting System Overview for you.

Your weapon is made out of 5 modules. Each of them is responsible for different aspects of the weapon.
[olist]
[*] LightCells - define basic damage and color of weapon’s projectiles
[*] Coolers - define max heat before weapon will overheat and its cooling rate
[*] Triggers - define how your input is handled
[*] Barrels - define how bullet fly out from the weapon
[*] Magazines - define what type of projectile the weapon will shoot
[/olist]
You can combine them freely adjusting the weapon to your needs.

We’ve prepared a short video that explains in detail what each module does and provides some decent module combinations

[previewyoutube=SIZsi0LBjgs;full][/previewyoutube]
In case you prefer written text here is quick module overview with examples.

[h2]Light Cells[/h2]
Light Cells define basic damage and color of weapon’s projectile.

Every bot and projectile has its color. The damage is increased if projectile color is close to enemy color and decreased when they are mismatched. 

For example hitting magenta bot with yellow or cyan projectile inflicts minor damage but using magenta projectile increases it 3 times.

LightCells comes only in 3 primary colors (in BotHunter universe primary colors are: Cyan, Magenta and Yellow), but opponents can have primary or secondary colored armor. If the bot has secondary colored armor you need to use one of the primary colors it was made of to deal greater damage. For example hitting a red bot with cyan is hardly doing anything but using magenta or yellow will do the job.

[h2]Coolers[/h2]
Coolers define max heat before the weapon will overheat and its cooling rate.

Each shot increases the weapon's heat. If the heat is too high the weapon will overheat and you won’t be able to shoot until it cools down. Higher tier Coolers increase max heat allowing you to shoot longer before overheating. They are essential for more advanced weapons because upgrading other modules increases heat required for each shot.

[h2]Triggers[/h2]
Triggers define how your input is handled.

The best way to understand them is through examples. Currently there are 4 Triggers implemented:
[olist]
[*] Pistol Trigger - on click shoot one time
[*] Burst Trigger - on click shoot quick 3-shot salvo
[*] Rifle Trigger - on hold shoot constantly
[*] Heavy Trigger - on click make one powerful shot.  It requires greater cooldown between shots
[/olist]

[h2]Barrels[/h2]
Barrels define how projectiles fly out from the weapon.

Currently there are 3 Barrels implemented:
[olist]
[*] Simple Barrel - shot one projectile
[*] Double Barrel - has two barrels. On the first shot launch one projectile from the first barrel, on the second shot use the other barrel and so on. This decreases cooldown between consecutive shots
[*] Shotgun Barrel - on one shot shoot multiple projectiles
[/olist]

[h2]Magazines[/h2]
Magazines define what type of projectile the weapon will shoot.

Currently there are 5 types of Magazines implemented:
[olist]
[*] Blaster - simple energy projectile
[*] Grenade - projectiles that explode after delay
[*] Mine - projectiles that explodes on enemy proximity
[*] Fireball - slow but powerful projectiles that explodes on contact
[*] Rocket - homing projectile that explodes on contact
[/olist]

That concludes all module types you can craft in Bot Hunter. Now it’s up to you how you will combine them to create your dream weapon. You can try it in the playtests we will be hosting soon. Stay tuned for more information!

Cheers!

notes.title: Dev Update #2
notes.notes:
Hello Hunters!

Since the last time you were hearing from us, a lot has changed in Bot Hunter. We managed to give our UI an overhaul. We have added a new death screen, which now shows the loss of items caused by the player's defeat. It also informs the player of the run time and the number of enemies killed. In addition to this, we have completely revamped the Quick Wheel menu and polished the Harbinger tab (i.e. the in-game chat). We also paid some extra attention to making our main menu look presentable by creating a Bot Hunters galaxy’s diorama and adding it to its background. 

This diorama can also be seen from the windows of our brand new hero ship that is finally fully functional. There, the player can access the Crafting Station and the Star Map, which is a holo version of Bot Hunter galaxy and is used to browse contracts and travel to different planets. 

When killing bots on the enemy's ship, you may notice that a new enemy has been added. We decided to call it Dragonfly because of its unique design - a dragon’s head and insect’s body. This enemy breathes fire and, like the insect from which it takes its name, can fly. However, we haven’t forgotten our old enemy types - we have given them freshly designed weapons to effectively stop the player from destroying their ships. 

To spice up the bot hunting we have added 4 new arenas, experimenting a bit with limiting space to the narrow corridors. We have also added 2 new boss arenas, each requiring the player to take a slightly different approach. But players will also be more powerful from now on, as we have completed the implementation of the Hack System. On the way through enemy’s ships in certain arenas you can see Hack Panels. When you approach them you can select one of two available hacks (i.e. perks) to boost your abilities for the rest of the run.

But you don’t have to remember all of this now as we have made a tutorial to teach you game mechanics of the game before you get into serious bot hunting. The tutorial includes specially prepared training arenas with tips on each of our game mechanics and its graphic representation if you’re not keen on reading.

Now we are getting ready for the demo release so stay tuned and follow our social media for more updates on Bot Hunter’s journey!

For those who have made it to the end of this dev update we have prepared a BONUS! Here’s a Bot Hunter’s gameplay footage of the entire run that shows all of the improvements listed above!

[previewyoutube=EEe6CQamz2c;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Dev Update #1
notes.notes:
Hello Hunters!

During the last couple of weeks we were super busy polishing our game for the trailer release. 

Our main focus was to increase UI readability. We improved crafting and weapon panels as well as map and minimap view. We reworked crosshair and added the heat bar which informs you about overheating your weapon. And lastly, we’ve added a custom death screen. 

For a smoother gaming experience we’ve implemented Xbox controller support. We adjusted UI navigation and added AimAssist which can be tweaked in the settings. DualSense support will be implemented in the nearest future. 

We were also working on bot design to increase coherency in the game. Each bot is now made of three parts: gray mechanical core, white armor plating and some extra elements that match the ship’s theme. Ships themselves vary in colors depending on the planet they’re from. 

With all the above we’ve updated our Steam page and managed to put together Bot Hunter’s announcement trailer. Check it out on our YouTube channel and follow us on social media for more updates on Bot Hunter’s journey!

[previewyoutube=Y9nUp7r06yc;full][/previewyoutube]
